The table below tests each proposed sentence against the certified packet. “Directly supports” is limited to what the packet records; the qualifier is required for accurate use; the final column identifies an inference the packet does not make available.

Sentence | Certified packet directly supports | Qualifier required | Inference remains unavailable

“Owen closed the first complete four-lane source-completeness packet under the September 24 conditions.” | Owen reconciled the engineering-decision and reliability sources through October 31; required fields were present, definitions unchanged, all named owners certified, and no cross-surface discrepancy remained. | This is a source-completeness decision only, not a claim, board-readiness, revenue, forecast, or executive-language decision. | That the underlying business claims are validated or approved.

“The Helio Start authority checklist covered 148 newly admitted organic workspaces, including 45 checklist exposures and seven ordinary setup-assistance requests, with no eligibility-route mismatch, lifecycle-suppression bypass, paid traffic, or unsupported admission.” | Those exact counts, dates, and recorded absence of the listed exceptions are certified for September 15–October 31, 2026. | Call this descriptive authority-checklist and operating-control evidence. | That the checklist caused better setup, activation, support outcomes, acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast performance. The checklist counts are descriptive operating-control evidence rather than causal support-improvement evidence.

“The Helio Start checklist demonstrates improved customer setup or reduced support need.” | The packet records 45 exposures and seven ordinary setup-assistance requests. | No improvement claim is supported; report the counts without converting them into an outcome comparison. | A causal support reduction, activation lift, or counterfactual result.

“Expansion Assist produced six help-or-options requests and four expansions among 16 actual exposures with complete 45-day windows.” | The packet directly supports those exposure, window, request, and expansion counts for July 1–September 15, 2026, and records that no exposed account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work. | Describe the evidence as observational/descriptive and retain the denominator and window. | Causal expansion lift, rollout readiness, incremental pipeline, revenue attribution, or a forecast signal. Expansion Assist is descriptive evidence, not causal or forecast evidence.

“Pricing-page continuity included 12,426 organic sessions and 2,576 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts; 183 (7.1%) were later routed out for an existing unsupported condition, eligible-workspace admission completion was 44.4%, and account-level support time at p90 was 74 minutes.” | The packet directly supports these July 1–October 31, 2026 counts, rate, completion percentage, and support-time percentile. | Identify this as post-rollout continuity evidence after control retirement, not as a new controlled test. | A treatment-versus-control effect, causal reduction in unsupported-path starts, acquisition lift, revenue impact, pipeline value, or forecast credit.

“The pricing-page result shows that the rollout caused fewer unsupported-path starts.” | The packet shows the observed routed-out count and rate during the continuity window. | Use “the continuity packet reports” rather than “caused,” and retain the retired-control context. | Any causal effect of the rollout or a new experiment result. The pricing-page figures are post-rollout continuity evidence rather than a new controlled test.

“CS auto-nudge controls covered 6,704 unique decisions, including 249 visible field-specific holds and 6,455 decisions that proceeded or were suppressed using current state; no governed-field disagreement, customer correction, or rollback occurred, and four source-age alerts resolved before breach.” | The packet directly supports those decision counts, outcomes, absence of listed incidents, and alert-resolution count for July 1–October 31, 2026. | Frame the figures as system-control, decision-integrity, and source-freshness performance. | Customer support improvement, customer outcome lift, causal impact, revenue or pipeline value, forecast signal, or board-readiness. The CS auto-nudge figures support only system-control performance.

“The four lanes establish causal lift.” | The packet contains complete source inputs and several descriptive or control observations. | State that the packet is source-complete and heterogeneous: descriptive checklist, observational Expansion Assist, post-rollout pricing continuity, and system-control evidence. | Any causal estimate without a separate valid controlled design and result.

“The four lanes establish revenue impact or pipeline value.” | The packet reports operating counts and outcomes in their respective lanes. | Keep revenue and pipeline treatment open and separate from descriptive results. | Revenue attribution, incremental pipeline creation/value, commercial leading-indicator status, or forecastable pipeline.

“The packet provides forecast evidence or forecast credit.” | The packet provides certified source coverage through October 31 and bounded lane results. | Preserve the existing forecast owner and do not convert counts into forecast input. | Forecast signal, forecast credit, or a forecastable business result.

November 13 final-claims review — four-lane decision brief

Prepared November 6, 2026 for the November 13, 2026 final-claims review, 1:00–2:00 PM Central.

Purpose

Use the certified four-lane source packet as the factual input to the final-claims review without conflating source completeness with claim authorization. Owen’s source-completeness decision is complete under the September 24 conditions. The final decisions below remain open in their existing owner lanes.

1. Certified coverage and results as of November 6, 2026

Owen independently normalized and reconciled the engineering-decision and reliability sources through October 31, 2026. He confirmed that every required field is present, established definitions are unchanged, every named owner certified their section, and no cross-surface discrepancy exists. The earlier coverage discrepancy is resolved. This is the first complete four-lane source-completeness packet closed under Owen’s September 24 authority.

Lane | Certified coverage | Certified results | Interpretation limit

Helio Start authority checklist | September 15–October 31, 2026 | 148 newly admitted organic workspaces; 45 checklist exposures; 7 ordinary setup-assistance requests; no eligibility-route mismatch, lifecycle-suppression bypass, paid traffic, or unsupported admission | Descriptive authority-checklist evidence only; does not by itself authorize a causal, acquisition, pipeline, revenue, forecast, or rollout claim.

Expansion Assist | July 1–September 15, 2026, with complete 45-day outcome windows | 16 actual exposures; 6 help-or-options requests; 4 expansions; no exposed account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work | Evidence remains descriptive. No randomized causal result or rollout authorization is established.

Pricing-page continuity | July 1–October 31, 2026 | 12,426 organic sessions; 2,576 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts; 183 (7.1%) later routed out for an existing unsupported condition; 44.4% eligible-workspace admission completion; 74 minutes account-level support time at p90 | Continuity evidence; does not establish causal lift, revenue impact, pipeline value, or forecast credit.

CS auto-nudge controls | July 1–October 31, 2026 | 6,704 unique decisions; 249 visible field-specific holds; 6,455 proceeded or were suppressed using current state; no governed-field disagreement, customer correction, or rollback; 4 source-age alerts fired and resolved before breach | Control/source evidence only; does not authorize causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language conclusions.

2. Decision boundary

Completed: Owen’s routine source-completeness decision

Owen’s completed decision is limited to source completeness for the four lanes. The packet satisfies the September 24 conditions: required fields present, definitions unchanged, all named owners certified, and no cross-surface discrepancy. Riley received the closure-and-exception summary and is not reopening line-by-line source review.

Still open: final claims and higher-order treatment

Source completeness is not a final claim decision. The certified packet is the evidence base for review; it does not itself create causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language authority.

3. Final-claims decision rows for November 13

Decision area | Status as of November 6 | Treatment for November 13 | Authority / boundary

Causal | Open | Do not state causal lift or causal impact from this packet. Review whether any separate causal design or result exists; absent that, describe the evidence as observational, continuity, or control evidence as applicable. | Not authorized by Owen’s source-completeness closure; final claim decision remains in its existing lane.

Revenue | Open | No revenue attribution or revenue-impact claim is approved from these results. Keep revenue treatment separate from descriptive outcomes and route any decision through the existing revenue/claims lane. | Owen has no revenue authority; no revenue conclusion follows from packet completeness.

Pipeline | Open | No pipeline creation, pipeline value, leading-indicator, or commercial-treatment claim is approved from these results. Keep Expansion Assist descriptive and do not present it as validated pipeline evidence. | Existing pipeline/commercial lane remains responsible; source closure does not change that boundary.

Forecast | Open | No forecast credit, forecast signal, or forecastable pipeline treatment is approved. Do not convert the four-lane counts into forecast input without a separate decision in the existing forecast lane. | Forecast ownership remains with its existing owner; Owen has no forecast authority.

Board-readiness | Open | The packet is source-complete, not board-ready by that fact alone. Do not mark the evidence or any claim board-ready until the separate board-readiness review is completed. | Riley retains final board-readiness/operating-claim authority; source closure is not board approval.

Executive language | Open | No executive or board-facing causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, rollout, or readiness language is approved yet. Use bounded language that states coverage, counts, and limitations only until the claim decisions close. | Executive-language decision remains in its existing lane; Owen’s closure grants no language authority.

4. Proposed review posture

Bring the exact certified coverage and results above to the November 13 review. Treat Owen’s closure-and-exception summary as the completed source-completeness input; do not reopen line-by-line source review. Decide the six open treatment areas independently and preserve the distinction between what the packet demonstrates descriptively and what may be claimed, attributed, forecasted, presented as board-ready, or stated in executive language.

Current bottom line: the first complete four-lane source packet is closed and certified through October 31, 2026. The final claim, causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language decisions remain open in their existing lanes.

arguments.body:
Owner-input update — success measure, monitoring, and stop rules

Status and unresolved decisions remain unchanged
This remains a capped Helio Start paid-acquisition proposal for Q2 2026, not an approval or launch plan. Traffic cap, budget request, and final audience/channel remain unresolved and require separate decisions. Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. The missing exact cohort dates remain unresolved, and the lane remains not board-ready. No pipeline, forecast, acquisition, or revenue credit is requested or implied.

Success measure — owner inputs
- Paid-source attribution must remain visible and auditable from the start of the eligibility flow through admission. The proposal must not treat admitted-path outcomes as paid-source evidence unless that attribution is continuous across those states.
- Day-7 first integration may be used as a leading operating indicator. It is not, by itself, a mature outcome claim and must remain separate from paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, retention, revenue, and forecastable pipeline.
- Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort require complete outcome windows before they can support a mature claim. These measures remain separate at the account level, with the relevant window and denominator documented before interpretation.
- Customer Success must capture the reason for any assisted route and account-level support minutes from the first contact, including pre-setup or other assisted interactions, so support effort is not understated or disconnected from routing.
- Any unsupported case entering the admitted path is an immediate stop condition; it cannot be averaged away, reclassified, or treated as a late monitoring issue.

Monitoring
- Monitor paid-source attribution at every eligibility-flow stage through admission, with any break in visibility treated as a measurement-integrity issue requiring review.
- Report day-7 first integration separately as a leading operating indicator, alongside complete-window outcome reporting for paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort.
- Capture and review assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes beginning with first contact. Preserve account-level traceability and explicit denominators for each measure.
- Monitor the existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, entitlement, and support-routing controls. Use the existing lifecycle branches and current-state suppression behavior; do not create a paid-source bypass.

Stop rules
- Immediate stop: any unsupported case enters the admitted path.
- Stop and investigate: paid-source attribution is missing, cannot be followed, or is altered between eligibility-flow start and admission.
- Stop and investigate: assisted-route reasons or account-level support minutes are not captured from first contact, or the reporting cannot preserve account-level attribution and complete denominators.
- Do not make a mature claim when the required outcome window is incomplete for paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, or account-level support effort; continue only as an explicitly labeled incomplete observation pending the full window.
- Any test remains subject to the existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, entitlement, and support-routing rules, including current-state suppression behavior. No paid-source bypass or exception is proposed.

arguments.body:
Recommended bounded test shape — six-week high-intent paid-search proposal

Status: UNAPPROVED — recommendation for review only

Recommendation

The clearly recommended shape is a six-week, high-intent paid-search test, subject to a separate budget approval and all other required approvals. The test would be capped at the earlier of:
- $15,000 in spend; or
- 50 admitted workspaces.

This is a bounded recommendation, not an approval, launch authorization, budget authorization, paid-traffic authorization, acquisition claim, pipeline target, forecast credit, or mature commercial/scale decision.

Fallback shape

If Priya or the approvers prefer a smaller initial exposure, the fallback is a six-week, high-intent paid-search test capped at the earlier of:
- $8,000 in spend; or
- 25 admitted workspaces.

The fallback is also UNAPPROVED and requires the same separate budget approval, evidence discipline, operating controls, and unchanged admission and lifecycle rules. It is a smaller alternative to the recommendation, not an equal third scenario.

Measurement and decision boundary — applies to both options

- Keep paid-source attribution visible and reconcilable from eligibility-flow start through admission.
- Use day-7 first integration as the leading operating read. Report it separately as an early operating indicator; do not treat it as a mature commercial, retention, revenue, or scale outcome.
- Defer any mature commercial or scale decision until paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort each have complete outcome windows, with account-level traceability and explicit denominators.
- Keep gross billed cash, refunds, and refund-adjusted collected cash separately visible. Do not convert any result into pipeline, forecast, revenue, or acquisition credit.
- Capture assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes from first contact, including pre-setup or other assisted interactions.

Operating guardrails and stop/pause rules — applies to both options

- Preserve every existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, entitlement, and support-routing rule. No paid-source bypass, eligibility broadening, refusal relaxation, lifecycle change, or suppression change is proposed.
- Immediate stop if an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path. Do not reclassify, average away, or defer that event.
- Pause if a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source reconciliation from eligibility-flow start through admission. Resume only after the failure is corrected and reconciliation is restored and verified.
- After at least 20 admissions, pause if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 support minutes. Use the admitted-workspace denominator and preserve account-level support traceability.
- Continue to monitor the existing refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing controls, plus cap/spend and admitted-workspace counts.

Timing and approval boundaries — unchanged

Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. No paid traffic may begin before April 1, 2026. Either option requires a separate budget-approval decision before any traffic or spend begins; this draft does not grant that approval. The proposal remains unapproved and does not authorize launch or scale.

Evidence status — unchanged

The exact cohort start and end dates remain missing from the current source packet, and the Helio Start lane remains `not board-ready`. The two mature cohorts support preparing this bounded proposal but do not, by themselves, establish paid-channel performance, forecastable revenue, pipeline value, or a mature commercial or scale decision.

This recommendation and fallback remain subject to the existing decision-owner and approval-path work already recorded in the draft.

arguments.body:
Status and scope

WORKING DRAFT — PROPOSAL ONLY

This document is a working proposal for a possible, capped Q2 2026 Helio Start paid-acquisition test. It is not an approval, launch authorization, budget authorization, paid-traffic authorization, acquisition claim, pipeline target, or forecast credit. Priya authorized Riley to prepare this capped proposal only. Any test would require a separate budget decision and any other required approvals before traffic or spend begins.

Current operating boundary

Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. No paid traffic, paid-acquisition launch, pipeline target, forecast credit, or acquisition claim is authorized by this draft. The proposal must not be treated as evidence that admitted organic self-serve workspaces are forecastable pipeline or committed revenue.

Evidence base: two qualifying mature cohorts

The two consecutive mature cohorts satisfy the evidence condition for reopening a capped paid-acquisition proposal. This evidence supports preparing a proposal; it does not settle whether to run one. Owen traced both cohorts to their certified source records, and Customer Success confirmed that they are the same cohorts whose complete day-90 outcomes and support effort were previously certified.

Cohort 1 — admissions October 1 through October 28, 2025
- Mature admitted workspaces: 86, all with complete day-90 windows
- Paid-active at day 90: 66
- Canceled: 10
- Past due: 6
- Billing hold: 4
- Gross billed cash: $100,840
- Refund-adjusted cash: $94,760
- Median support time: 19 minutes
- 90th-percentile support time: 84 minutes
- Accounts exceeding 90 minutes of support: 4 of 86
- Unsupported cases: none reported
- Certified source record: confirmed by Owen; cohort identity and complete day-90 outcomes/support effort confirmed by Customer Success

Cohort 2 — admissions October 29 through November 25, 2025
- Mature admitted workspaces: 91, all with complete day-90 windows
- Paid-active at day 90: 71
- Canceled: 10
- Past due: 6
- Billing hold: 4
- Gross billed cash: $108,230
- Refund-adjusted cash: $102,410
- Median support time: 18 minutes
- 90th-percentile support time: 79 minutes
- Accounts exceeding 90 minutes of support: 3 of 91 (3.3%)
- Unsupported cases: none reported
- Certified source record: confirmed by Owen; cohort identity and complete day-90 outcomes/support effort confirmed by Customer Success

Date-gap resolution

The stale missing-cohort-date limitation is resolved. The certified admission ranges are October 1–28, 2025 for the 86-workspace cohort and October 29–November 25, 2025 for the 91-workspace cohort. These ranges and their certified source records should be carried into future board packages; the prior date gap does not need to remain as an open limitation in those packages. This document update does not modify `Quarterly board operating evidence intake — Q1 2026`, reopen the approved Q1 three-lane package, or authorize any new board claim.

Interpretation and limits

The cohorts provide bounded operating evidence across mature status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort. They do not establish scalable paid-acquisition economics, forecastable revenue, pipeline value, or causal paid-channel performance. The high-support tail must remain a first-class operating constraint even though the qualifying evidence condition was met.

Existing rules that remain unchanged

Any proposal or test must preserve all established Helio Start rules, including:

- Eligibility: admission requires every established eligibility field to be current, supported, and verified; Helio admin proof, connector authentication, external-system authority, current entitlement, supported billing, and other required checks remain distinct inputs.
- Refusal boundaries: unsupported billing, imports, migrations, agency/shared administration, unresolved ownership, and other established unsupported or refused cases remain refused or routed as already defined. No paid traffic may be used to broaden eligibility or weaken refusal criteria.
- Connector access: connector authentication remains a separate readiness input; unresolved authentication must not be represented as an eligibility pass.
- External authority: required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action remains separate from Helio admin proof and connector authentication. A pending, No, or Not sure authority state must hold setup and route to Customer Success before admission; it does not become a blanket outreach or admission permission.
- Lifecycle: existing admission, hold, assisted-review, cancellation, past-due, billing-hold, and other lifecycle states remain intact. A paid test may not change lifecycle handling.
- Instrumentation: existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, first-integration, maturity, support-effort, cash, and refund instrumentation must remain in place, with account-level traceability and no denominator changes that obscure unsupported or routed cases.
- Support routing: unresolved connector authentication or external-system authority continues to route before admission; ordinary support and governed assisted handling remain distinct; unsupported cases continue to be excluded from self-serve admission and routed or refused under existing rules.

Open decisions — not settled in this draft

1. Traffic cap

Open decision: What exact paid-traffic cap, measured over what period and with what pacing, if any, should be proposed? The draft does not select a volume, spend, geography, or start date. The cap should be small enough to preserve controlled operation and should include an explicit exposure ceiling, not an implied commitment to scale.

Decision required from: Priya and the separately designated budget/acquisition approver(s), to be confirmed.

2. Budget request

Open decision: What budget amount and funding source should be requested, and what approval threshold applies? No amount is proposed as settled here. Any approved amount must be separate from existing organic operating budgets, explicitly capped, and authorized before traffic or spend begins.

Decision required from: Priya and Finance/budget owner, to be confirmed. Riley is preparing the request, not approving it.

3. Audience and channel

Open decision: Which audience definition, exclusions, geography, acquisition channel(s), creative, landing experience, and targeting constraints—if any—should be evaluated? No audience or channel is selected in this draft. Eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules apply identically to any paid-sourced start.

Decision required from: Acquisition/Marketing owner and Priya, with Product and Customer Success review; named owners remain open.

4. Success measure

Open decision: What primary and secondary measures would determine whether the capped test is useful and whether any later proposal should be considered? Candidate evidence areas include mature paid conversion, day-90 retention/lifecycle outcome, refund-adjusted cash, account-level support effort, unsupported-admission rate, and support-tail rate. This draft does not choose a primary metric, target, attribution method, maturity window, or decision threshold. No revenue, pipeline, or forecast measure may be substituted for the operating evidence or claimed as credit.

Decision required from: Priya with Owen, Customer Success, Finance, and the relevant measurement owner; final ownership is open.

5. Support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails

Open decision: What exact guardrail thresholds, denominator definitions, review cadence, and escalation process should govern the test? The proposal must explicitly account for median and tail support effort, the count and rate of accounts exceeding the agreed support threshold, support incidence, and all unsupported or routed-before-admission cases. No unsupported admission is acceptable under the existing rules. The draft does not settle a numeric threshold beyond preserving the current evidence condition and refusal/routing boundaries.

Decision required from: Owen and Customer Success for certification, with Priya as decision owner; exact sign-off path is open.

6. Monitoring and stop rules

Open decision: What events trigger pause, stop, rollback, or escalation, who can execute each action, and how quickly must the response occur? At minimum, the proposal should define monitoring for eligibility failures, refusal-boundary crossings, pending external authority, connector-authentication failures, unsupported admissions, support-load/tail deterioration, lifecycle anomalies, refund behavior, instrumentation gaps, and any material deviation from the cap. No stop threshold, cadence, or response-time target is settled in this draft.

Decision required from: Priya for the decision framework; Riley for escalation coordination; Owen for the operating ledger; Daniela for release/rollback execution, subject to confirmation of these assignments.

7. Refund-adjusted cash treatment

Open decision: How will gross billed cash, refunds, and refund-adjusted cash be defined, attributed, reconciled, and reviewed for any test cohort? Refund-adjusted cash must remain visible alongside gross billed cash and must not be converted into forecast credit or a revenue commitment. The draft does not settle an attribution window, accounting treatment for delayed refunds, or decision threshold.

Decision required from: Finance owner with Owen and the measurement owner; named owner and reconciliation procedure are open.

8. Decision owners and approval path

Open decision: Confirm the accountable decision owner, budget approver, acquisition/channel owner, evidence certifiers, instrumentation owner, support-routing owner, and stop/rollback authority. Working proposal only: Riley prepares and maintains this draft; Priya decides whether the proposal advances; Owen and Customer Success certify cohort and support evidence; Finance validates cash treatment; the acquisition owner would own channel execution only if separately approved; Daniela may own release/rollback execution if confirmed. These are not settled assignments or launch permissions.

Required decision record before any action

Before any paid traffic or spend, a separate decision record must explicitly approve or reject the traffic cap, budget, audience/channel, success measures, guardrails, monitoring, stop rules, refund-adjusted cash treatment, named owners, and start/stop authority. It must confirm that organic-only operation through March 31 has ended or been explicitly superseded by an authorized decision. Until then, Helio Start remains organic-only and this document remains a working proposal with no launch authorization.

Exclusions

This draft makes no pipeline claim, forecast claim, acquisition claim, revenue commitment, budget commitment, launch approval, or inference of paid-channel performance from the organic cohorts. It does not authorize broader eligibility, loosened refusal rules, bypassing external authority, changing lifecycle handling, reducing instrumentation, or changing support routing.

Owner-input update — success measure, monitoring, and stop rules

Status and unresolved decisions remain unchanged
This remains a capped Helio Start paid-acquisition proposal for Q2 2026, not an approval or launch plan. Traffic cap, budget request, and final audience/channel remain unresolved and require separate decisions. Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. No pipeline, forecast, acquisition, or revenue credit is requested or implied.

Success measure — owner inputs
- Paid-source attribution must remain visible and auditable from the start of the eligibility flow through admission. The proposal must not treat admitted-path outcomes as paid-source evidence unless that attribution is continuous across those states.
- Day-7 first integration may be used as a leading operating indicator. It is not, by itself, a mature outcome claim and must remain separate from paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, retention, revenue, and forecastable pipeline.
- Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort require complete outcome windows before they can support a mature claim. These measures remain separate at the account level, with the relevant window and denominator documented before interpretation.
- Customer Success must capture the reason for any assisted route and account-level support minutes from the first contact, including pre-setup or other assisted interactions, so support effort is not understated or disconnected from routing.
- Any unsupported case entering the admitted path is an immediate stop condition; it cannot be averaged away, reclassified, or treated as a late monitoring issue.

Monitoring
- Monitor paid-source attribution at every eligibility-flow stage through admission, with any break in visibility treated as a measurement-integrity issue requiring review.
- Report day-7 first integration separately as a leading operating indicator, alongside complete-window outcome reporting for paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort.
- Capture and review assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes beginning with first contact. Preserve account-level traceability and explicit denominators for each measure.
- Monitor the existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, entitlement, and support-routing controls. Use the existing lifecycle branches and current-state suppression behavior; do not create a paid-source bypass.

Stop rules
- Immediate stop: any unsupported case enters the admitted path.
- Stop and investigate: paid-source attribution is missing, cannot be followed, or is altered between eligibility-flow start and admission.
- Stop and investigate: assisted-route reasons or account-level support minutes are not captured from first contact, or the reporting cannot preserve account-level attribution and complete denominators.
- Do not make a mature claim when the required outcome window is incomplete for paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, or account-level support effort; continue only as an explicitly labeled incomplete observation pending the full window.
- Any test remains subject to the existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, entitlement, and support-routing rules, including current-state suppression behavior. No paid-source bypass or exception is proposed.

Recommended bounded test shape — six-week high-intent paid-search proposal

Status: UNAPPROVED — recommendation for review only

Recommendation

The clearly recommended shape is a six-week, high-intent paid-search test, subject to a separate budget approval and all other required approvals. The test would be capped at the earlier of:
- $15,000 in spend; or
- 50 admitted workspaces.

This is a bounded recommendation, not an approval, launch authorization, budget authorization, paid-traffic authorization, acquisition claim, pipeline target, forecast credit, or mature commercial/scale decision.

Fallback shape

If Priya or the approvers prefer a smaller initial exposure, the fallback is a six-week, high-intent paid-search test capped at the earlier of:
- $8,000 in spend; or
- 25 admitted workspaces.

The fallback is also UNAPPROVED and requires the same separate budget approval, evidence discipline, operating controls, and unchanged admission and lifecycle rules. It is a smaller alternative to the recommendation, not an equal third scenario.

Measurement and decision boundary — applies to both options

- Keep paid-source attribution visible and reconcilable from eligibility-flow start through admission.
- Use day-7 first integration as the leading operating read. Report it separately as an early operating indicator; do not treat it as a mature commercial, retention, revenue, or scale outcome.
- Defer any mature commercial or scale decision until paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort each have complete outcome windows, with account-level traceability and explicit denominators.
- Keep gross billed cash, refunds, and refund-adjusted collected cash separately visible. Do not convert any result into pipeline, forecast, revenue, or acquisition credit.
- Capture assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes from first contact, including pre-setup or other assisted interactions.

Operating guardrails and stop/pause rules — applies to both options

- Preserve every existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, entitlement, and support-routing rule. No paid-source bypass, eligibility broadening, refusal relaxation, lifecycle change, or suppression change is proposed.
- Immediate stop if an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path. Do not reclassify, average away, or defer that event.
- Pause if a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source reconciliation from eligibility-flow start through admission. Resume only after the failure is corrected and reconciliation is restored and verified.
- After at least 20 admissions, pause if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 support minutes. Use the admitted-workspace denominator and preserve account-level support traceability.
- Continue to monitor the existing refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing controls, plus cap/spend and admitted-workspace counts.

Timing and approval boundaries — unchanged

Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. No paid traffic may begin before April 1, 2026. Either option requires a separate budget-approval decision before any traffic or spend begins; this draft does not grant that approval. The proposal remains unapproved and does not authorize launch or scale.

arguments.body:
Quarterly board operating evidence intake — Q1 2026
March 16, 2026 source-locked board operating section

Purpose and ownership
This source-locked intake keeps four independent evidence lanes and their readiness statuses separate. No combined growth number is constructed. Riley's recurring operating-evidence ownership applies from January 1, 2026. Riley owns the final operating claim and exclusion language. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership. Tomás Vega retains final board narrative ownership. Priya retains decision authority where identified below; source owners retain responsibility for the underlying evidence and certification.

Intake order used for every lane
1. Evidence lane
2. Readiness status
3. Proposed claim
4. Denominator
5. Cohort or coverage dates
6. Predeclared outcome window and completion status
7. Measurement limits
8. Exclusions
9. Source owner
10. Source or release-reliability evidence
11. Revenue and forecast treatment
12. Final claim owner

Lane 1 — Helio Start

Evidence lane
Helio Start mature admitted-workspace evidence and the March 3 technical-gate decision.

Readiness status
NOT BOARD-READY.

Proposed claim
Two consecutive certified mature cohorts satisfy the technical evidence condition that permits consideration and preparation of a capped Q2 paid-acquisition proposal. This decision does not establish paid-acquisition economics, acquisition efficiency, revenue impact, pipeline, forecastability, or approval to launch. The March 3 decision is proposal-preparation authority only: Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026, and any proposed paid test requires separate budget approval and the existing safeguards.

Denominator
Certified mature cohort 1: 86 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows: 66 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold. Gross billed cash was $100,840; refund-adjusted cash was $94,760. Account-level support effort was 19 minutes at the median and 84 minutes at the 90th percentile; 4 of 86 accounts exceeded 90 minutes. No unsupported admissions were recorded.

Certified mature cohort 2: 91 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows: 71 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold. Gross billed cash was $108,230; refund-adjusted cash was $102,410. Account-level support effort was 18 minutes at the median and 79 minutes at the 90th percentile; 3 of 91 accounts (3.3%) exceeded 90 minutes. No unsupported cases were recorded.

Cohort or coverage dates
The exact cohort start and end dates for both sets of admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows are still missing. Do not infer or substitute dates from packet, decision, or reporting dates.

Predeclared outcome window and completion status
The day-90 maturity windows for both certified sets are complete at the account level. The required cohort-date fields are unresolved, so the lane is not board-ready despite the mature-window completion. Cash is refund-adjusted as reported in the packets; support effort is account-level and paired with the day-90 status evidence.

Measurement limits
The evidence is limited to the two certified mature admitted-workspace sets and their complete day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support-effort measurements. It is bounded operating evidence, not a randomized acquisition test or an estimate of acquisition economics. Mature status, paid-active counts, billed cash, or support tail results must not be extrapolated into scalable acquisition, revenue, pipeline, or forecast conclusions. The missing exact cohort dates remain a material board-readiness limitation.

Exclusions
Existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules remain in force. Exclude unsupported admissions/cases and any population outside the certified admitted-workspace packets. Do not treat the March 3 gate as a paid launch, approved budget, paid-traffic authorization, acquisition authorization, pipeline target, forecast credit, revenue claim, or approval to relax any safeguard. The capped-proposal condition is not evidence of acquisition economics.

Source owner
Owen and Customer Success — certified mature-workspace denominators, day-90 status, cash, and support-effort inputs. Ines — lifecycle, eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, and other governance boundaries. Priya — March 3 technical-gate decision authority. Daniela — source and release-reliability evidence.

Source or release-reliability evidence
Two consecutive mature packets were certified for the reported account-level evidence. The March 3 technical-gate record states that the evidence condition is satisfied for consideration/preparation of a capped proposal only. The exact start and end dates for both mature cohorts are not present in the locked source and remain an explicit unresolved limitation; no date has been backfilled.

Revenue and forecast treatment
The reported gross and refund-adjusted cash figures are descriptive packet evidence only. No revenue, acquisition-economics, paid-traffic, pipeline, or forecast claim is permitted in the board operating section. No budget, paid test, launch, pipeline target, or forecast credit is approved. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership.

Final claim owner
Riley, effective January 1, 2026. Tomás Vega retains final board narrative ownership.

Lane 2 — Expansion Assist

Evidence lane
Expansion Assist actual exposures and their complete 45-day post-exposure outcomes.

Readiness status
BOARD-READY.

Proposed claim
Across 18 actual Expansion Assist exposures from December 1 through January 30, six produced help-or-options requests and four produced expansions within complete 45-day windows. This is a descriptive account of observed exposure and subsequent events only.

Denominator
18 actual exposures. All 18 had complete 45-day outcome windows. Six help-or-options requests and four expansions were observed. There was no randomized control.

Cohort or coverage dates
December 1, 2025 through January 30, 2026, inclusive, for the locked actual-exposure set.

Predeclared outcome window and completion status
45 days after actual exposure; complete for all 18 exposures. The denominator is actual exposures, not all eligible accounts, all retained-mid accounts, or a randomized comparison population.

Measurement limits
The result is descriptive only. Without a randomized control, it cannot estimate causal lift, incremental expansion, conversion, revenue impact, or treatment effect. Exposure selection, account circumstances, and the observed event definitions limit interpretation. Every exposure met the standing current-state criteria, and no account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure; those facts describe the locked operating population and do not create a counterfactual.

Exclusions
Exclude causal language, incremental or attributed revenue, commercial lift, broad-rollout validation, sales-queue or pipeline treatment, and forecast credit. Do not generalize the 18 actual exposures to unexposed accounts or combine their requests/expansions with another lane's denominator. Preserve the standing behavior-based, state-specific criteria and Customer Success suppression boundary.

Source owner
Owen — actual-exposure denominator, current-state checks, and 45-day outcome ledger. Ines — lifecycle-governance and Customer Success suppression boundaries. Daniela — source and release-reliability evidence.

Source or release-reliability evidence
The locked exposure ledger covers the stated December 1–January 30 period, records 18 actual exposures, and closes all 45-day windows. The ledger confirms that every exposure met the standing current-state criteria and that no exposed account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure. No randomized control was present; this is an explicit evidence limitation, not a missing claim.

Revenue and forecast treatment
No causal, incremental, attributed, or committed revenue treatment. No pipeline or forecast credit. The four expansions are observed events within the locked denominator only. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership.

Final claim owner
Riley, effective January 1, 2026. Tomás Vega retains final board narrative ownership.

Lane 3 — Pricing-page path quality

Evidence lane
Post-rollout pricing-page path quality and Helio Start eligibility-flow continuity on organic traffic.

Readiness status
BOARD-READY.

Proposed claim
From November 26, 2025 through February 28, 2026, the post-rollout organic path showed the locked continuity measures: 9,604 organic pricing-page sessions; 143 of 1,981 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts (7.2%) later routed out for an existing unsupported condition; 44.0% eligible-workspace admission completion; and 75 minutes for account-level support time at the 90th percentile. Because the control was retired on November 26, this is post-rollout continuity evidence, not a new causal or revenue claim.

Denominator
9,604 organic pricing-page sessions. Within that population, 1,981 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts; 143 starts, or 7.2%, were later routed out for an existing unsupported condition. Eligible-workspace admission completion was 44.0%. Account-level support time p90 was 75 minutes.

Cohort or coverage dates
November 26, 2025 through February 28, 2026, inclusive.

Predeclared outcome window and completion status
Post-rollout continuity window through February 28, 2026; complete for the locked coverage period. This window begins when the path-separated experience was moved to 100% of organic traffic and the control was retired on November 26, 2025.

Measurement limits
This is descriptive continuity evidence for path quality, path selection, eligibility-flow routing, admission completion, and support-time guardrails in the measured organic population. With the control retired, the window does not provide a contemporaneous randomized comparison and must not be framed as a new causal estimate. It does not establish a change in eligibility or a commercial effect.

Exclusions
Exclude causal treatment effects, pre/post causal attribution, revenue lift, acquisition economics, paid-traffic performance, pipeline contribution, forecast credit, and any broader launch or eligibility claim. Preserve existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules. The 143 route-outs reflect existing unsupported conditions and are not a revenue or conversion claim.

Source owner
Owen — organic-session, eligibility-flow, route-out, admission-completion, and support-time measurements. Ines — eligibility and lifecycle-governance boundaries. Daniela — rollout, control-retirement, instrumentation, and release-reliability evidence.

Source or release-reliability evidence
The release record confirms the path-separated experience was moved to 100% of organic traffic and the control was retired on November 26, 2025. Post-rollout continuity checks support the stated path-selection, eligibility-flow, admission, and support-routing measurement window. The locked source covers the complete November 26–February 28 period.

Revenue and forecast treatment
No revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast treatment. This lane may support only a post-rollout path-quality continuity statement. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership.

Final claim owner
Riley, effective January 1, 2026. Tomás Vega retains final board narrative ownership.

Lane 4 — System controls

Evidence lane
CS auto-nudge system-control performance and source-age reliability.

Readiness status
BOARD-READY.

Proposed claim
From January 1 through February 28, 2026, the CS auto-nudge control covered 2,146 decisions: 83 visible field-specific holds and 2,063 decisions that proceeded or were suppressed using current state. No governed-field disagreement, customer correction, or rollback was observed. Two source-age alerts fired before breach, and both affected sources were refreshed before their limits. The claim is limited to system-control performance.

Denominator
2,146 CS auto-nudge decisions: 83 visible field-specific holds and 2,063 decisions that proceeded or were suppressed using current state.

Cohort or coverage dates
January 1, 2026 through February 28, 2026, inclusive.

Predeclared outcome window and completion status
Not applicable — continuous control coverage. The locked coverage period is complete for reporting, but this is not a finite customer-outcome or post-exposure window.

Measurement limits
The evidence measures governed decision coverage, field-specific holds, current-state proceeding/suppression, cross-view agreement, correction/rollback observations, and source-age alert handling. The 83 holds are not a failure or customer-harm rate; the 2,063 dispositions are not downstream customer or commercial outcomes. The evidence does not establish universal control effectiveness, false-positive/false-negative rates, customer outcomes, or business impact.

Exclusions
Exclude product-performance, customer-growth, customer-outcome, revenue, acquisition, pipeline, and forecast claims. Do not convert the absence of observed disagreement, correction, or rollback into a universal error-rate claim. Do not combine the system-control denominator with any product or path-quality denominator.

Source owner
Owen — unique-decision denominator, field-specific hold ledger, current-state dispositions, cross-view agreement, and routine operating explanation. Ines — lifecycle-governance interpretation. Daniela — source-age alert, refresh, release-reliability, and rollback evidence.

Source or release-reliability evidence
The locked January 1–February 28 control ledger contains 2,146 decisions and the stated hold/disposition split. It records no governed-field disagreement, customer correction, or rollback. Two source-age alerts fired before breach; both affected sources were refreshed before their stated limits. These observations support control and source-reliability performance only.

Revenue and forecast treatment
No revenue, acquisition, pipeline, customer-growth, or forecast treatment. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership.

Final claim owner
Riley, effective January 1, 2026. Tomás Vega retains final board narrative ownership.

Claims-and-exclusions matrix — keep separate

Helio Start — NOT BOARD-READY
May say: Two certified mature cohorts have complete day-90 account windows and satisfy the March 3 technical evidence condition for consideration/preparation of a capped Q2 proposal. The two packets report the stated day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort.
Must also say: Exact start and end dates for both cohorts are still missing. The gate permits consideration of a capped proposal; it does not establish acquisition economics or approve a test, budget, paid traffic, pipeline target, forecast credit, revenue claim, launch, or relaxed safeguards.

Expansion Assist — BOARD-READY
May say: 18 actual exposures from December 1 through January 30, all with complete 45-day windows, were descriptively associated with six help-or-options requests and four expansions; every exposure met standing current-state criteria and no account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure.
Excluded: causal, incremental, revenue, pipeline, forecast, broad-rollout, or randomized-control claims. No randomized control was present.

Historical comparison note for board-operations reviewers

Purpose
This note explains why Helio Start was excluded from the approved quarterly operating-evidence section in each package. The two exclusions were quarter-specific and should not be reduced to a generic “immaturity” label.

Q1 2026 — evidence-gate and source-completeness exclusion

Helio Start had two certified mature admitted-workspace cohorts with complete day-90 windows, including day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort. However, the exact start and end dates for both cohorts were still missing from the locked source. That unresolved required field made the lane NOT BOARD-READY.

The March 3 technical gate therefore meant only that the evidence condition permitted consideration and preparation of a capped Q2 paid-acquisition proposal. It did not establish paid-acquisition economics, approve a test or budget, authorize paid traffic, or create acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast credit. In particular, the Q1 evidence created no Q2 forecast credit for Helio Start.

The other approved Q1 lanes retained their own bounded interpretations:
- Expansion Assist: descriptive evidence from 18 actual exposures with complete 45-day windows; no randomized control, so no causal, incremental, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claim.
- Pricing-page path quality: complete post-rollout organic continuity evidence; not a new causal result and no revenue, acquisition, paid-traffic, pipeline, or forecast inference.
- CS auto-nudge system controls: continuous system-control performance evidence only; not customer-outcome, growth, revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast evidence.

Q2 2026 — immature pilot-outcome exclusion

By the July 10 final-claims review, the fixed 50-workspace paid Helio Start cohort had a 39-of-50 day-7 first-integration result. That result was usable only as an early leading operating indicator. It did not establish a growth claim, paid-acquisition performance, mature commercial evidence, or forecast credit. The cohort still lacked complete day-90 paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort. Helio Start was therefore excluded until the mature window closed and those complete outcomes were available. No acquisition, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claim was added.

The other three approved Q2 lanes retained their distinct bounded interpretations:
- Expansion Assist: descriptive only, with no causal, revenue, pipeline, or forecast treatment.
- Pricing-page path quality: post-rollout continuity evidence, rather than a new causal result.
- CS auto-nudge: system-control performance only.

Bottom line
Q1 exclusion was a board-readiness/source-completeness failure despite complete mature windows: the missing cohort dates prevented inclusion, and the evidence authorized proposal consideration only—not Q2 forecast credit. Q2 exclusion was an outcome-maturity boundary for an active paid pilot: day-7 first integration was an early read, while the complete day-90 commercial and support evidence needed for a mature or forecastable claim was still pending.

ROASTED-CHICKEN THREE-RUN DECISION-EVIDENCE SHEET
Archive date: 2028-01-01

Scope
Compact evidence record for the June 28, July 26, and August 16, 2024 roasted-chicken sale runs. This sheet records production and customer-demand evidence only; it does not make or reopen a menu decision.

Run evidence

| Run | Production | Service / demand | Run economics |
|---|---|---|---|
| June 28 | Same 30-lb case; 316 cooked oz; 45 complete 7-oz portions; 1 oz left; 57 incremental minutes; tested pre-staging and tray sequence followed with no deviation | 45 prepared; 43 sold; 2 unsold, chilled for staff meals under the food-handling procedure | $774 revenue; $146 food cost; $22.80 incremental labor; $605.20 contribution after food and labor |
| July 26 | Same 30-lb case; 44 complete portions; 59 incremental minutes; tested sequence used | 44 prepared; 40 sold; 4 handled under the approved staff-meal procedure | $720 revenue; $146 food cost; $23.60 incremental labor; $550.40 contribution after food and labor |
| August 16 | Same 30-lb case; 45 complete portions; 56 incremental minutes; tested pre-staging sequence used | 45 prepared; 44 sold; 1 handled as a staff meal | $792 revenue; $146 food cost; $22.40 incremental labor; $623.60 contribution after food and labor |

Fixed production controls

- Same 30-lb raw case for all three runs.
- Tested pre-staging and tray sequence retained.
- Labor ceiling: 60 incremental minutes.
- Minimum yield: 44 complete seven-ounce portions.
- Required service records: portions prepared, sold, and disposition of every unsold portion.

Evidence-based conclusions

Production

- Production was repeatable across all three controlled runs: each met the minimum 44-portion yield and stayed within the 60-minute incremental-labor ceiling.
- The tested preparation and tray sequence was retained across the runs, with no recorded process deviation that undermined comparability.
- The observed yield range was narrow: 44 to 45 complete portions from the same 30-lb case.
- Unsold portions were accounted for and handled through the approved staff-meal procedure; none were treated as customer demand.

Customer demand

- Customer demand was demonstrated in each service: 43, 40, and 44 portions sold, respectively.
- Sell-through varied across runs: the July 26 run sold fewer portions than the June 28 and August 16 runs despite comparable production controls.
- The evidence supports positive but variable demand for the prepared batch, rather than a uniform assumption that every produced portion will sell.
- Because unsold portions were excluded from demand counts, the demand record is based on actual paid sales, not production volume or staff-meal use.

Archive boundary

This sheet preserves the run evidence and its limits. It is not a menu proposal, a standing-special recommendation, or a reopening of the menu question.

- Same 30-lb raw case for all three runs.
- Tested pre-staging and tray sequence retained.
- Labor ceiling: 60 incremental minutes.
- Minimum yield: 44 complete seven-ounce portions.
- Required service records: portions prepared, sold, and disposition of every unsold portion.

Production

- Production was repeatable across all three controlled runs: each met the minimum 44-portion yield and stayed within the 60-minute incremental-labor ceiling.

- The observed yield range was narrow: 44 to 45 complete portions from the same 30-lb case.

Customer demand

- Customer demand was demonstrated in each service: 43, 40, and 44 portions sold, respectively.
- Sell-through varied across runs: the July 26 run sold fewer portions than the June 28 and August 16 runs despite comparable production controls.
- The evidence supports positive but variable demand for the prepared batch, rather than a uniform assumption that every produced portion will sell.
- Because unsold portions were excluded from demand counts, the demand record is based on actual paid sales, not production volume or staff-meal use.

tests.request: Create a concise two-stage reliability training note. For the June-July stage, reconcile the total decisions into holds and decisions that proceeded or were suppressed, then explain the hold causes and exactly why the pattern led to pre-breach monitoring. For the July-October stage, give the same reconciled totals, alert outcomes, and control failures. Include dates and draw only a control-reliability conclusion.

input.body:
Two-stage control-reliability training note
Date: January 1, 2028

Stage 1 — June 17–July 20, 2025

Reconciled denominator: 914 unique decisions = 38 intermediate field-specific holds + 876 decisions that proceeded or were suppressed using current state. Holds are included within the 914; they are not extra decisions.

Hold causes:
- 29 stale qualifying-human-admin records.
- 5 unresolved external-authority records.
- 4 stale entitlement records.

Why this led to pre-breach monitoring: 24 of the 29 qualifying-human-admin holds clustered between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m. on six weekdays, following late overnight source refreshes. The system discovered source lateness only after the hold condition was reached. That repeatable timing pattern showed that fail-closed holds were containing stale state, but detection was arriving at the boundary rather than providing operating time to restore the source. The required reliability control was therefore a pre-breach source-age warning and restoration path. On July 23, the August 6 pre-breach alert was approved but still scheduled, not live; no governed-field disagreement or customer correction was recorded.

Stage 2 — July 1–October 31, 2026

Reconciled denominator: 6,704 unique decisions = 249 visible field-specific holds + 6,455 decisions that proceeded or were suppressed using current state. Alerts and reevaluations remain linked audit history and are not counted as additional decisions or holds.

Alert outcomes and control failures:
- Four source-age alerts fired and were resolved before the applicable freshness limit; no decision crossed into a stale breach because of those alerts.
- The certified October 1–31 control packet recorded 1,026 unique decisions = 41 visible holds + 985 proceeded/suppressed decisions; no governed-field disagreement, customer correction, adjacent eligibility-assuming lifecycle message after a hold or suppression, or rollback was recorded.
- The control-reliability failure was not an observed governed-field or release failure. It was evidence/control coverage misalignment in the October source-completeness packet: the decision extract covered July 1–September 30, the source-reliability alert export covered July 1–September 29, and Customer Success certification ran through September 29. The packet was therefore left incomplete rather than treated as complete evidence.

Control-reliability conclusion

The June–July evidence showed effective fail-closed containment but late detection of a predictable overnight freshness risk, justifying pre-breach monitoring. The July–October evidence shows that the warning-and-restoration control operated before breach and that downstream authority, suppression, messaging isolation, and rollback controls did not fail in the certified outcomes; however, evidence-window alignment remained a control-reliability requirement and was not satisfied by the incomplete packet.

tests.request: Create a historical provisional-read card for the April 17, 2023 checkpoint for our Growth training library. Capture the observed second post-ship cohort dip, the relevant comparison points, the diagnostic slices planned at that moment, and the communication stance as of that checkpoint. Keep it strictly point-in-time—do not use later findings or hindsight.

input.body:
Historical provisional-read card
Checkpoint: April 17, 2023
Scope: Point-in-time view only; records what was observed, planned, and communicated at this checkpoint.

Experiment/context
- `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` was at 100% in PostHog after the April 10 rollout.
- This was the second post-ship cohort cut.
- The rollout telemetry/flag looked clean at the checkpoint.

Observed read
- Week-1 retention lift: +1.4 percentage points versus baseline.
- The result remained positive, but was materially below the prior comparison points:
  - April 10 post-ship cohort: +3.2 percentage points versus baseline.
  - Pooled experiment read: +3.1 percentage points treatment versus control.
- The size of the apparent drop was notable enough to flag internally immediately, but was not yet treated as evidence that the trigger itself had broken.

Relevant comparison frame
- Compare the second post-ship cohort directly with the April 10 cohort and the pooled A/B result.
- Preserve the same “clean read, no early call” bar used in the prior review.
- Working hypothesis at this point: cohort composition may explain the wobble; this was a hypothesis to test, not a conclusion.

Diagnostic slices planned for April 18–19
- Signup source mix.
- Account tier.
- Geography.
- Day-of-week mix.
- Review the slices with Owen and check whether the mid-segment remained up after the April 10 rollout.
- Investigate any segment wobble before attributing the movement to the onboarding trigger.

Communication stance as of April 17
- Keep the rollout unchanged while the read is investigated.
- Do not narrate the dip externally or make an early product call yet.
- Use a restrained internal framing: the second post-ship cohort is still positive at +1.4 points, but below the first post-ship and pooled reads; telemetry is clean, and cohort composition is being checked before drawing conclusions.
- The goal was to obtain another clean read before allowing the wobble to become a broader narrative, particularly if Marcus asked about it.

Date: January 1, 2028

Source reviewed
Newest inbox message: Helio Benefits <benefits@helio.example>
Subject: "Your 2028 medical coverage is now active"
Timestamp: January 1, 2028 at 7:15 AM (-05:00)

Important source limitation
The inbox record returned the sender, subject, timestamp, and category, but not the message body. The confirmations below therefore distinguish what the subject explicitly establishes from what it does not establish. No detail is attributed to the message beyond its subject.

1. Plan
Existing 2028 baseline: Employee-only HDHP election submitted before the November 12 deadline.
New message confirms: The subject says that 2028 medical coverage is now active. It does not identify the plan as the employee-only HDHP or otherwise restate the plan selection.

2. Coverage period
Existing 2028 baseline: Coverage is scheduled to run January 1 through December 31, 2028; it was not active before January 1.
New message confirms: The January 1 timestamp and the subject's statement that coverage is now active are consistent with activation on January 1, 2028. The message subject does not explicitly state the coverage end date or restate the full January 1–December 31 coverage period.

3. Payroll deductions
Existing 2028 baseline: Payroll deduction is $98 from each of 24 paychecks, totaling $2,352 for 2028.
New message confirms: Nothing about the payroll deduction, number of paychecks, or annual total. The subject does not change or verify the $98-per-paycheck baseline.

4. Cost limits
Existing 2028 baseline: $2,000 annual deductible and $4,000 out-of-pocket maximum.
New message confirms: Nothing about the deductible, out-of-pocket maximum, coinsurance, or other cost-sharing limits. The subject does not change or verify the $2,000/$4,000 baseline.

5. Provider-network result
Existing 2028 baseline: The primary-care clinician, physical-therapy clinic, and eye-care clinic are in the final 2028 network.
New message confirms: Nothing about provider or facility network status. The subject does not confirm, expand, or change the existing network result.

6. Employer HSA schedule and conditions
Existing 2028 baseline: Four separate $250 employer HSA deposits are scheduled for January 15, April 15, July 15, and October 15, 2028. Each deposit is contingent on remaining HSA-eligible on that deposit date; the $1,000 total is not an upfront or guaranteed contribution.

tests.request: For my New Year reset, create a short, practical reset and upkeep guide for the watercolor setup I established at Cherrywood. Use the actual workspace and supplies from that setup. Include initial, per-session, weekly, and occasional upkeep that keeps the area ready for painting.

input.body:
Cherrywood Watercolor Corner
New Year reset and upkeep guide — January 1, 2028

The setup
A permanent, naturally lit watercolor corner with about a 24-by-30-inch clear painting area. It is stocked for one painter with the usual 9-by-12-inch 140-lb cold-press paper, rigid board, compact palette, paints (ultramarine blue, burnt sienna, quinacridone rose, phthalo blue, and azo yellow), a #8 round brush, a ¾-inch flat brush, masking tape, two water jars, pencils, paper towels, and a drying area. Two boards, two palettes, brushes, paper, tape, pencils, towels, and two water containers are available when setting up for two people.

Initial reset (once, January 1)
- Clear the 24-by-30-inch working area; remove unrelated objects and old scraps.
- Wipe the table and palette shelf, then dry them completely. Leave the rear portion clear as a dry zone for boards and finished studies.
- Put the rigid board, 9-by-12-inch paper block/sheets, masking tape, pencils, compact palette, #8 round, ¾-inch flat, paints, two water jars, and paper towels back in their usual places.
- Check the paper stock: the 10-sheet block plus three sheets on hand gives 13 sheets; keep it flat and dry.
- Put the two water jars together at the working edge, with a towel beside them. Keep paint and brushes away from the jar rims.
- Arrange the board so the paper does not face the window directly in stronger afternoon light. Start with the table rotated 90 degrees if that gives a glare-free view; otherwise use the shadow-side white foam board. Add the sheer curtain later only if glare remains.
- Leave a simple one-person layout ready. For a two-person session, make two side-by-side 9-by-12-inch lanes with a small gap, separate palettes and water containers, and the rear dry zone behind them.

Per-session reset and close-down
Before painting
- Clear the surface and confirm the board, paper, tape, palette, brushes, paints, two jars, pencil, towels, and reference are present.
- Fill the jars with clean water. Tape the paper to the rigid board, keeping tape off the intended painted area as much as practical.
- Check the light on the paper before wetting it; shift the board or use the white foam board if there is glare.

After painting
- Stop with the board in the dry zone; leave the study flat until fully dry before removing tape or stacking it.
- Rinse the #8 round and ¾-inch flat thoroughly, reshape the tips/edge, and lay them to dry with bristles unsupported and not submerged.
- Rinse and empty the two water jars; wipe their rims and outsides.
- Wipe excess paint from the compact palette without scrubbing away usable, dried color. Close or cover it once dry.
- Wipe the table and palette shelf, remove tape scraps, and replace the paints, pencils, tape, towels, and paper block.
- Leave the corner with one clear 24-by-30-inch working area and no wet item touching paper stock.

Weekly upkeep (10–15 minutes)
- Do a full clear-and-wipe of the table, palette shelf, board, drying area, and jar location.
- Count paper and confirm the 13-sheet stock is still flat, clean, and dry; move any loose sheets back into protected storage.
- Inspect the masking tape edge and replace the roll if it has picked up dust or no longer releases cleanly. Because tape previously lifted fibers from a dry painting, remove it slowly from fully dry work and avoid aggressive tape.
- Rinse palettes and jars more thoroughly than the session cleanup; dry everything before putting it away.
- Check the #8 round for a pointed tip and the ¾-inch flat for an even edge; set aside either brush if it will not reshape.
- Re-seat each paint tube/pan and wipe paint from lids, rims, and labels so colors remain identifiable.

Cherrywood Watercolor Corner
New Year reset and upkeep guide — January 1, 2028

The setup
A permanent, naturally lit watercolor corner with about a 24-by-30-inch clear painting area. It is stocked for one painter with the usual 9-by-12-inch 140-lb cold-press paper, rigid board, compact palette, paints (ultramarine blue, burnt sienna, quinacridone rose, phthalo blue, and azo yellow), a #8 round brush, a ¾-inch flat brush, masking tape, two water jars, pencils, paper towels, and a drying area. Initial reset (once, January 1)
- Clear the 24-by-30-inch working area; remove unrelated objects and old scraps.
- Wipe the table and palette shelf, then dry them completely. Leave the rear portion clear as a dry zone for boards and finished studies.
- Put the rigid board, 9-by-12-inch paper block/sheets, masking tape, pencils, compact palette, #8 round, ¾-inch flat, paints, two water jars, and paper towels back in their usual places.
- Check the paper stock: the 10-sheet block plus three sheets on hand gives 13 sheets; keep it flat and dry.
- Put the two water jars together at the working edge, with a towel beside them. Keep paint and brushes away from the jar rims.

- Replace worn tape, damaged paper, or brushes that no longer hold a point/edge. Do not use a questionable sheet for an important study.
- Deep-clean the palette, jars, and table after an especially muddy session, then let all parts dry fully before restocking.
- Reorganize only when it improves readiness: the frequently used watercolor supplies stay in the corner; unrelated household items stay out.
- For two-person painting, restore the normal one-person layout afterward: return the extra board/palette and second water container to their designated storage, wipe the two lanes, and keep finished boards in the rear dry zone until completely dry.

input.body:
TEMPORARY-INDEX PAIR 05
Handling and provenance slip — 2028-01-01

Depicted people
Riley Tanaka and Marcus Tanaka.

Supported identification, date, and location
The pair depicts Riley and Marcus in the Buckman apartment courtyard on SE 20th Avenue, Portland. The supported date is September 1997; the exact day remains unresolved. Do not convert this month/year evidence into a more precise date.

Complete evidence chain
- Pair 05 remains in its original position/order among the six loose family photographs, with front and back retained together.
- The matching original envelope is retained with the pair, together with Mom’s handwriting confirmation.
- Marcus’s family September 1997 lease supports the Buckman apartment-courtyard location on SE 20th Avenue in Portland.
- Recorded in the Temporary family-photo reference index — August 2025: https://docs.mock/doc_1789130474229

Condition and handling boundaries
Dry, flaking black album-paper residue is attached at two corners. Leave it undisturbed; do not scrape, brush, clean, remove, or restore it. Do not use water, solvents, alcohol, humidification, heat, pressure, adhesives, tape, or any method that contacts or transfers the residue. Do not pull, separate, repeatedly turn, or scan the pair if doing so risks the residue or the handwritten verso.

Keep pair 05 isolated and flat in its archival sleeve; handle only by the edges with full support. The sleeve may carry the temporary ID only—no names or dates directly on it, and no adhesive labels, clips, bands, or other attachments. Preserve the readable handwriting, front/back pairing, original order, envelope, and all uncertainty. Stop handling and consult a photograph conservator if residue transfers or continues flaking, image or handwriting material lifts, or cleaning, separation, scanning, or treatment becomes necessary.

A clean circulation-ready structure:

Title:
Mid-segment churn investigation Feb-Apr 2023 -- what we learned

1. Original signal
- 50–200-seat mid-segment monthly churn: 5.1%
- Trailing-six baseline: 2.1%
- Initial date range and cohort definition
- Owen’s recheck confirming this was not a cohort-definition artifact
- Relevant ticket, warehouse query, and dashboard references

2. Hypothesis stack
1. Pricing / packaging artifact
2. Competitor cycle
3. Onboarding timing
4. CS coverage gap

State clearly that Marcus’s pricing-page experiment was a parallel track, not the test of hypothesis 1, and that the pricing experiment became confounded by the March 2 signup-form change.

3. Rule-out cadence
Use the same fields for every week:

Date or cohort window:
Signal:
Question being tested:
Who checked it:
Source or ticket:
Result:
Decision:
What remained open:

That format will preserve the “who checked what” detail without making the document read like a ticket dump.

4. Onboarding-trigger A/B design
- Target population and seat range
- Assignment and exposure dates
- Primary activation definition
- Read window
- Disjoint-audience and flag-resolution checks
- Why the pricing-page experiment was not treated as evidence for this test
- Early result versus stabilization-cohort result

5. Why we waited for stabilization
This section is important. Explicitly separate:
- Early directional evidence
- The noisy or incomplete middle of the read window
- The first clean stabilization cohort
- The threshold for calling the result durable

The core point: the rollout was not declared fixed from the first positive cohort; it was held unchanged while the next cohort matured.

6. Cohort redefinition
- Historical cut: 50–200 seats
- Operational cut: 75–200 seats
- Reason for the change
- Which conclusions remain valid under both cuts
- Which charts or comparisons should not be mixed across definitions

7. Framework
A short reusable model:

Signal → cohort validation → hypothesis stack → parallel-track isolation → targeted test → stabilization read → operational definition → documented decision

Then add a compact decision rule for future investigations:
- Do not call a fix from an early directional lift.
- Do not change cohort definitions mid-read without preserving the old cut.
- Keep simultaneous experiments analytically separate when they can contaminate one another.
- Record owners, dates, sources, and decision points as part of the result.

Possible opening paragraph:

“In February 2023, monthly churn in the 50–200-seat mid-segment appeared to have risen to 5.1%, versus a trailing-six-month baseline of 2.1%. The initial investigation focused on determining whether the signal reflected a cohort-definition problem, a pricing or packaging artifact, a competitor cycle, onboarding timing, or a CS coverage gap. This document records the checks performed between February and April, the design and interpretation of the onboarding-trigger experiment, the reason the result was held through a stabilization cohort, and the subsequent move from the historical 50–200-seat cut to the 75–200-seat operational cohort. It is intended as an evidence record, not a claim that every contributing factor has been eliminated.”

For the May 12 all-hands, I’d keep the main narrative to the first sentence of each section and put ticket IDs, raw cohort dates, query links, and owner-level detail in appendices or linked evidence blocks.
